scope: A new population assumption for the qualifying-derived track factor at a circuit absent from the training catalogue; not an inferred posterior for its physical characteristics.
reference: Keep the fixed training factor's origin and units. Its eligible training values are scaled to unit spread by f1rank.design.circuit_factors, without mean centering. The neutral origin remains zero; do not recenter training factors or car states.
independence: New circuit coordinates are independent of each other and the fitted posterior conditional on its training design. Within a draw, use the same circuit coordinate with each paired team-season loading and its paired qualifying/race car link.
persistence: Reuse the circuit coordinate across visits and seasons within a trajectory, regardless of entrant order, forecast prefix or draw batching.
known_circuits: Retain the fitted fixed factor, including a zero factor selected by the existing insufficient-history convention. Uncertainty in learned training factors is not estimated by this extension.
short_training_history: A new joint-model circuit retains the specified population distribution even when the training factor axis is all zero. Its population spread is an assumption, not a scale learned from absent data; fitted loading uncertainty remains prior-dominated where appropriate.
race_only_ablation: Preserve the explicitly removed qualifying-derived axis at zero for every circuit. Do not inject a qualifying factor or its variation into that separately defined evidence ablation.
interface: Joint-model forecasts at unseen circuits require this policy explicitly. Omission rejects the forecast instead of choosing a fixed neutral factor. Known-circuit forecasts remain unchanged.
tuning: No real-event accuracy or ranking outcome selects this population law. Preserve failures; any revision requires a new declared version before evaluation.
remaining: Calibrate this extrapolation and the existing fixed-factor approximation; register circuit treatment for all arms before predictive evaluation. This does not repair uncertainty in the fitted training factors.
